hypothesis: If bivalve and brachiopod growth lines are coaxial curves through the umbo rather than concentric circles about an interior centre, then a published table of several plan-view growth lines on each valve will be fit more closely by circles that share one point on the outline than by circles that share one centre.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). An admissible file (defined in test_contract) yields at least 8 valves, each with at least 3 growth lines and at least 10 points on each line. For each valve, fit a concentric model (one shared centre, one radius per line) and a coaxial-circle model (one shared point that every line passes through, centres free) by least squares on the radial residual. Supported if, for at least 80 percent of valves, the median absolute residual of the coaxial model is less than half the median absolute residual of the concentric model.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (claim refuted). Refuted if at least 8 admissible valves are measured and fewer than 40 percent of them have a coaxial median absolute residual less than half the concentric residual. If the fraction is at least 40 percent and below 80 percent, the verdict is mixed. If no admissible coordinate table is retrieved, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. Adult length and height, a single outline per valve, a radial cross-section through the shell thickness, an image that would have to be traced, and any login-gated scan are not admissible and do not count toward the 8 valves.

test_contract.expected_observation: On valves with several digitized plan-view growth lines, a model of circles through one shared umbonal point leaves a median absolute residual less than half that of a concentric-circle model, on at least 80 percent of at least 8 valves.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The concentric model fits as well or better on most valves: fewer than 40 percent of at least 8 valves meet the half-residual rule. That is the pattern of growth lines centred inside the valve rather than coaxial through the umbo.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Openly downloadable numeric coordinates, no login, of the plan-view generating curve of a bivalve or brachiopod valve, with at least three growth lines per valve. The lines must be measurements already published as coordinates, not traced for this test from a photograph or a plate. A longitudinal or radial section through shell thickness is a different curve and is not admissible. A single adult outline, or length and height alone, cannot separate coaxial from concentric and is not admissible.
test_contract.inference_method: Least-squares radial residuals of a concentric-circle family versus a coaxial-circle family on the same points. The verdict is the fraction of valves whose coaxial residual is less than half the concentric residual, with the thresholds in pass_criterion and fail_criterion. Named genera (Anomia, Lima, Solen) are reported if present and are not required for the verdict.

interpretation: Thompson's coaxial circles are the Galileo family: every growth line passes through the umbo, and the centres lie on a line. Concentric circles share a centre and do not all pass through one boundary point. The adult outline always meets the umbo, so one outline cannot decide the question. The axis ratios he gives for Anomia (about 1), Lima subauriculata (vertical about twice transverse) and Solen pellucidus (transverse three to four times vertical) describe the shape of those curves; they are not a substitute for the coaxial-versus-concentric comparison. His printed table of ellipse chords is his own calculation, not a measurement of shells, and is not data for this test.
caveats: MorphoSource is named by both assessors. A previous attempt stalled because media download requires a login. This registration does not treat a login-gated scan as a retrieved dataset.

The following were identified from landing pages and descriptions only, before any coordinate file for this claim was downloaded: de Winter's Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1045192 supplement is a longitudinal cross-section of one Magallana gigas shell; Neubauer's PANGAEA 10.1594/PANGAEA.810112 files are one outline per venerid valve; the sclero shellspots object is a shell section; Shackleton's Dryad 10.5061/dryad.j4n09 scallop file is adult landmarks; the El Dornajo table is length and height. None of these is admissible under the contract. The analysis script re-checks the URLs and does not use their numbers.
No plan-view growth-line coordinate table was located during that search. If the script also finds none, the pre-registered verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
